Ghazi Diyan Baawan Lay Gaiyan, Zainab Da Muk Hy Maan Geya

Jaira Zaamin Paak Ridaawan Da, Oh Veer Toh Ho Qurbaan Geya

Is Khabar Ne Seena Cheer Ditta, Abbas Ne Mur Ke Aaona Nai
Raitan Wich Baazu Rul Jaanay, Kissay Laash Nu Vi Dafnaona Nai
Bethi Khaak Te Zainab Rondi Ay, Kitthay Pardeyan Da Nigraan Geya

Akhiyan Wich Tapdiyan Raitan Sarn, Zakhmaan Chon Khoon Vi Jaari Si
Ghazi De Sikh De Hotaan Te, Zainab Di Parda Dari Si
Jadon Laash Chawarn Pyu Jaaye Di, Kul Sabiraan Da Sultan Geya

Abbas Di Maut Te Lokaan Ne, Sehra Wich Jashan Manaaye Ne
Zahra De Laal De Sajde Wich, Teeran Ne Kitte Saaye Ne
Jiddi Aas Te Bhaina Baahr Aaiyan, Oh Maut Da Ban Mehmaan Geya

Tin Nokaan Wala Teer Jadon, Asghar De Gal Te Maareya Si
Masoom Sakina Ro Ro Ke, Chachay Ghazi Nu Pukareya Si
Do Ghut Paani De Waaste Hy, Ay Jhoola Ho Viraan Geya

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p = 'src/data/lyrics/ghazi-diyan-baawan-lay-gaiyan-nw-3b9e061be7de.md'
f = Path(p)
s = f.read_text()
s = s.replace('Raitaan wich', 'Raitan wich')
f.write_text(s)
_, meta, body = s.split('---', 2)
roman = meta.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)[1]
def verses(t):
    return [v.strip() for v in t.splitlines() if v.strip() and not v.strip().isdigit()]
old = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', f'HEAD:{p}'], text=True).split('---', 2)[2]
assert [v.casefold() for v in verses(roman)] == [v.casefold() for v in verses(old)]
for part in (roman, body):
    assert [len(verses(block)) for block in part.strip().split('\\n\\n')] == [2, 3, 3, 3, 3]
print('Verified 14 verses, original Roman wording, and matching stanza structure')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 14 verses in Punjabi Shahmukhi and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`. The verse grammar supports Punjabi, so I updated the language metadata. Both versions have a two-line preamble and four matching numbered stanzas.

I read the ambiguous Roman phrases `sikh de` and `chawarn` as `سُکدے` and `چھوڑن`, respectively.
